title: AI & Shopping
hook: AI can be a genuinely useful shopping assistant — comparing options, summarizing specs, finding deals. It's also quietly flooding stores with fake reviews and AI-invented products.
key_points: Helpful: comparing products, explaining specs, narrowing choices, drafting questions.
Recommendations are AI built to maximize sales, not necessarily your best interest.
Fake AI-written reviews are everywhere — read critically and check multiple sources.
Watch for AI-generated product images and listings that don't match reality.
content_html: Shopping is quietly becoming an AI-mediated experience, and it cuts both ways. On the helpful side, a chatbot can be a surprisingly good shopping assistant: paste in two products and ask it to compare them, have it explain what a spec actually means in practice ("do I need this many watts?"), narrow a huge field down to a few sensible options for your needs, or draft the questions to ask before a big purchase. Retailers' own AI can also surface relevant items and bundle information in genuinely convenient ways.
extra_html: The catch is that a lot of the AI in shopping is working for the seller, not for you — and some of it is working for scammers. Recommendation engines are tuned to maximize sales and time-on-site, so "recommended for you" means "likely to make us money," which isn't always your best or cheapest option. More corrosively, AI has made fake reviews trivial to mass-produce: glowing, fluent, human-sounding praise generated by the thousand to prop up mediocre or fraudulent products. AI-generated product photos and entire listings can misrepresent what actually shows up at your door. The defenses are old-fashioned but effective: read reviews critically (be suspicious of a flood of generic five-stars or oddly similar phrasing), check ratings across more than one site, look for detailed reviews with real photos, and be extra wary of unknown sellers and deals that seem too good. Let AI help you understand your options — then judge the source before you trust the praise.

related.title: AI in Everyday Tools
related.hook: You've used AI for years without calling it that — every time your phone unlocks with your face, your maps reroute around traffic, or your inbox filters spam.

related.title: Spotting AI-Made Content
related.hook: There are real tells for AI text and images — but they're fading fast, and 'AI detector' tools are unreliable. The durable skill is judging the source, not squinting at the pixels.

related.title: AI Scams & Staying Safe
related.hook: AI didn't invent scams — it just made them cheaper, faster, and far more convincing. The good news: the habits that beat them haven't changed.

flashcards.prompt: What's a growing problem for online shoppers in the AI era?

choices.text: Fake AI-written reviews and AI-generated listings that mislead buyers
Stores refusing to use any AI

flashcards.explanation_html: AI makes it cheap to mass-produce convincing fake reviews and even fake product images, so reviews and listings need a more skeptical eye than ever.

flashcards.prompt: Whose interest does a store's AI recommendation really serve?
flashcards.back_html: Primarily the seller's — recommendation engines are optimized to maximize sales and engagement, which doesn't always line up with your best buy.
